# The Veil That Reveals the Light

## Scripture
"He wraps himself in light as with a garment; he stretches out the heavens like a tent." — Psalm 104:2

## Reflection
Tonight, if you're fortunate enough to stand beneath a truly dark sky, you may witness the Milky Way—that great river of starlight arcing across the heavens. It appears as a luminous veil, a soft white glow that seems almost like smoke or mist. Yet we know the truth: that "veil" is the gathered light of hundreds of billions of stars, so distant they blur together into a single band of radiance.

There's a holy irony here. The very darkness that hides individual stars is what reveals the greater glory of the galaxy. The interstellar dust that obscures our view of the galactic core also scatters and reflects light, painting that breathtaking ribbon across the night.

How often do we mistake obscurity for absence? When God seems hidden behind the "dust" of our circumstances, we assume He has withdrawn. But perhaps He is simply wrapping Himself in a different garment—one that requires our eyes to adjust, our faith to stretch. The psalmist tells us God clothes Himself in light. Even the darkness that hides Him is part of His wardrobe, woven to reveal His glory in ways brilliance alone never could.

## Prayer
Father of endless light, when I cannot see You clearly, teach me to trust the veil. Help me remember that Your hiddenness is never Your absence—only Your invitation to look deeper, wait longer, and believe brighter. Amen.
